content: Insulin therapy or other glucose-lowering treatments should be initiated or intensified in hospitalized adults if persistent hyperglycemia is observed with blood glucose levels at or above 180 mg/dL (10.0 mmol/L), as confirmed by at least two separate readings. For the majority of hospitalized patients, the recommended target blood glucose range is between 140-180 mg/dL (7.8-10.0 mmol/L). In critically ill patients, a more stringent blood glucose target range of 110-140 mg/dL (6.1-7.8 mmol/L) may be appropriate, provided that it can be achieved safely without increasing the risk of hypoglycemia.
